The program is designed for working professionals.
Typically, candidates complete the program within 8 to 9 semesters (includes summer term).
The curriculum is structured into three main components: Foundation Coursework, Methods & Application Coursework, and the Internship.
Candidates may start the program in the fall, spring, or summer semesters, beginning with Foundation Coursework.
Both Foundation and Methods & Application Coursework must be completed before enrolling in the Internship course.
Clinical experiences are completed throughout the program, providing opportunities to integrate theory and practice in real world settings.
In order to accommodate working professionals, candidates will collaborate with the program coordinator to develop an individualized course sequence for their foundational coursework.

Candidates are required to take the following courses: Foundation Coursework EDC 529 Foundations of Educational Research EDL 500 Engaging Communities for Change EDL 501 Legal and Ethical Issues in Educational Leadership EDL 502 Fiscal Management for Educational Leaders EDL 503 Operations & Management for Educational Leaders Methods & Application Coursework EDL 504 Program Evaluation for School Leaders EDL 505 Supervision of Instruction EDL 506 Instructional and Curriculum Leadership EDL 507 Managing Human Capital EDL 508 Leading School & District Improvement Internship EDL 510 Internship I + Seminar EDL 511 Internship II + Seminar This program is considered a hybrid program.
Courses will be delivered online in a combination of synchronous (Zoom) and asynchronous (Brightspace) sessions.
A variety of instructional methods are used, including lectures, discussions, case studies, presentations, cooperative learning activities, Internet assignments, guest practitioner presentations (as possible), role-play, and written and verbal assignments.
Courses are taught by URI full-time and part-time faculty.

Program Learning Outcomes At the completion of this program, candidates will understand and demonstrate the capacity to promote the current and future success and well-being of each student and adult in their school community by applying the knowledge, skills, and commitments necessary to: Goal #1 - Strategic Leadership and Visioning 1.1 - Collaboratively lead, design, and implement a school mission, vision, and process for continuous improvement that reflects a core set of values and priorities, including data use, technology, equity, diversity, digital citizenship, and community. 1.2 - Demonstrate the capacity to advocate for ethical decisions and cultivate and enact professional norms. 1.3 - Develop and maintain a supportive, equitable, culturally responsive, and inclusive school culture.

Opportunities for Graduates The Educational Leadership & Policy (EDL) program at the University of Rhode Island equips graduates with the skills, knowledge, and credentials necessary to pursue a wide range of leadership roles within the education sector.
The program is designed to meet the growing demand for qualified school leaders, addressing both current workforce needs and future job market trends.
Economic Need and Workforce Data The demand for skilled educational leaders is increasing, particularly as schools and districts navigate complex challenges such as educational equity, technological integration, and community engagement.
According to the U.S.
Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), employment for elementary, middle, and high school principals is projected to grow by 4% from 2022 to 2032, which reflects the steady need for qualified individuals to fill these critical roles.
The BLS also highlights the ongoing need to replace retiring principals, further emphasizing the demand for new school leaders.
Available Jobs and Job Titles Graduates of the EDL program are well-prepared to assume a variety of leadership positions within the educational field.

Some of the common job titles for program graduates include: School Principal Assistant Principal Dean District Administrator Instructional Coordinator Director of Special Education Curriculum Director Superintendent These roles are crucial in shaping the educational experiences of students and ensuring that schools operate effectively and efficiently.
The EDL program provides the comprehensive preparation necessary for graduates to excel in these positions.
Job Outlook and Growth The job outlook for educational leaders is positive, particularly in urban centers and areas with growing student populations.
The Bureau of Labor & Statistics (BLS) projects that there will be about 20,000 openings for principals each year over the next decade, mostly due to workers leaving the labor force or transferring to other occupations.
Salaries Salaries for educational leadership positions vary depending on the role and geographic location, but they generally reflect the high level of responsibility associated with these roles.
According to the BLS, the median annual wage for elementary, middle, and high school principals was $103,310 as of May 2022.

District administrators and superintendents often earn higher salaries due to the increased scope of their responsibilities.

Demand For Program The Educational Leadership & Policy program at the University of Rhode Island is designed to prepare the next generation of educational leaders and policymakers.

As the landscape of education continues to evolve, there is a growing need for skilled leaders who can navigate the complexities of educational institutions, implement effective policies, and drive meaningful change.
Effective principals have substantial positive impacts on student achievement.
Research demonstrates that replacing a below-average principal with an above-average one can significantly increase student learning in both math and reading annually.
Beyond student achievement, principals also affect other crucial outcomes such as student attendance, discipline, and teacher retention.
Effective principals are linked to reduced absenteeism and exclusionary discipline, as well as higher teacher job satisfaction and lower turnover rates, particularly among high-performing teachers.
Principals who engage in instructionally focused interactions with teachers, such as providing feedback, coaching, and developing a data-driven instructional program, contribute to positive school outcomes.
These practices emphasize the importance of principals being deeply involved in the instructional aspects of their schools.
Principals play a crucial role in addressing educational equity.

Effective leaders are adept at creating inclusive environments that support diverse student populations.
This involves strategic hiring, fostering collaborative cultures, and ensuring equitable allocation of resources.
Rhode Island, like many other states, is facing a shortage of school administrators.
According to data collected by the Rhode Island Department of Education for the 2021-22 school year, 46 administrator vacancies were reported by 41 Local Education Agencies (LEAs), representing 8% of building-level administrator positions statewide.
Nationally, the National Center for Education Statistics (2023) found that about one in ten public school principals left the profession between the 2020-21 and 2021-22 school years.
This highlights the urgent need for strong principal preparation programs that equip future leaders with the skills required for effective school leadership.
Ongoing professional development and support are critical to ensure principals have the tools necessary to succeed (Grissom, Egalite, and Lindsay, 2021).
